questions.prompt_text: According to the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of “cloud computing,” what is the meaning of the statement “a shared pool of configurable computing resources”?

options.text: Networks, servers, storage, applications, and services.
Data security associated with data loss or unavailability causing business disruption.
Five essential characteristics, three deployment models, and three service models.
Leveraging cloud services over the open internet on hardware owned by the cloud provider.

questions.raw_block_text:
1.
Question 1

According to the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of “cloud computing,” what is the meaning of the statement “a shared pool of configurable computing resources”?

Do you understand?.

I understand

Networks, servers, storage, applications, and services.

Data security associated with data loss or unavailability causing business disruption.

Five essential characteristics, three deployment models, and three service models. 

Leveraging cloud services over the open internet on hardware owned by the cloud provider.

Nice work

Correct! NIST explicitly identifies these as the core "resources." In a cloud environment, these are pooled together so that multiple customers can draw from the same underlying hardware, configuring them to their specific needs via software.

1 / 1 point

questions.prompt_text: What tasks do hypervisors accomplish?

options.text: Enable multiple operating systems to run alongside each other and separate VMs logically
Fluctuates workloads and facilitates access to mainframes
Scale on demand to support fluctuating workloads
Facilitates access to mainframes, allowing multiple users to access the same data storage layer

questions.raw_block_text:
2.
Question 2

What tasks do hypervisors accomplish?

Do you understand?.

I understand

Enable multiple operating systems to run alongside each other and separate VMs logically

Fluctuates workloads and facilitates access to mainframes

Scale on demand to support fluctuating workloads

Facilitates access to mainframes, allowing multiple users to access the same data storage layer

Nice work

Correct! A hypervisor is the foundational "Virtual Machine Monitor" (VMM). It allows one physical server to host multiple independent virtual machines (VMs), ensuring that each OS thinks it has its own dedicated hardware while logically isolating them for security.

1 / 1 point

Question 4

According to the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of “cloud computing,” what is the meaning of the statement “a shared pool of configurable computing resources”?

Networks, servers, storage, applications, and services.

What tasks do hypervisors accomplish?

Do you understand?.

I understand

Enable multiple operating systems to run alongside each other and separate VMs logically

Fluctuates workloads and facilitates access to mainframes

Scale on demand to support fluctuating workloads

Facilitates access to mainframes, allowing multiple users to access the same data storage layer

Correct! A hypervisor is the foundational "Virtual Machine Monitor" (VMM). It allows one physical server to host multiple independent virtual machines (VMs), ensuring that each OS thinks it has its own dedicated hardware while logically isolating them for security.

Risk exposure

Infrastructure and workloads

Data security risks associated with the loss or unavailability of data

Business continuity

Lack of standardization in how the constantly evolving technologies integrate

Correct! Cloud providers utilize redundancy. If one physical hard drive or server fails, your data is already replicated across other machines in the data center, ensuring high availability and durability that is difficult to achieve on a single local computer.

Multi-cloud infrastructures

Data-driven decisions

To migrate applications to cloud-native microservices for faster and more reliable customer service

To expand their global presence and accelerate growth
